knowledge_point.title: Identifying Parallel Lines Given in Standard Form

question.:question/problem: Which of the following lines is parallel to $-4x-2y=-6$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For two distinct nonvertical lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of $-4x-2y=-6$, convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-4x-2y &= -6 \\
-2y &= 4x-6 \\
y &= -2x+3
\end{aligned}
$$

The slope is the coefficient of $x$, so the required slope is $-2$.

Only $y=-2x-1$ has slope $-2$.

The line $y=-2x-1$ has slope $-2$ and $y$-intercept $-1$, different from $3$. Therefore, it is a distinct parallel line.

$$
y=-2x-1
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following lines is parallel to $-4x-2y=-6$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For two distinct nonvertical lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of $-4x-2y=-6$, convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-4x-2y &= -6 \\
-2y &= 4x-6 \\
y &= -2x+3
\end{aligned}
$$

The slope is the coefficient of $x$, so the required slope is $-2$.

Rewrite the choices in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-6x-2y=0 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-3x \\
-x+y=2 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=x+2 \\
2x+y=-1 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-2x-1 \\
4x-y=3 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=4x-3 \\
-6x+3y=3 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=2x+1
\end{aligned}
$$

Only $2x+y=-1$ has slope $-2$.

The line $2x+y=-1$ has slope $-2$ and $y$-intercept $-1$, different from $3$. Therefore, it is a distinct parallel line.

$$
2x+y=-1
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following is a distinct line parallel to $-4x-2y=-6$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For two distinct nonvertical lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of $-4x-2y=-6$, convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-4x-2y &= -6 \\
-2y &= 4x-6 \\
y &= -2x+3
\end{aligned}
$$

The slope is the coefficient of $x$, so the required slope is $-2$.

Rewrite the choices in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-4x-2y=-6 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-2x+3 \\
-x+y=2 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=x+2 \\
2x+y=-1 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=-2x-1 \\
x-y=3 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=x-3 \\
-6x+3y=3 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad y=2x+1
\end{aligned}
$$

The line $-4x-2y=-6$ has both the same slope $-2$ and the same $y$-intercept $3$ as the given line. It is the same line, so it is not a distinct parallel line.

The line $2x+y=-1$ has slope $-2$ and $y$-intercept $-1$, different from $3$. Therefore, it is a distinct parallel line.

$$
2x+y=-1
$$
